itens.titulo: Nvidia stock extends $2.5 trillion rout as SEC probe reportedly investigates its accounting
itens.descricao: Nvidia stock extends $2.5 trillion rout as SEC probe reportedly investigates its accounting Yahoo Finance
trechos: Nvidia (NVDA) stock is down about 10% Friday, on track for its worst day since the DeepSeek rout in January 2025 and its seventh straight loss.
Nvidia is shedding about $400 billion in market value Friday and is on track to lose more than $750 billion this week.
That would top the $573 billion it lost last week, the biggest one-week drop for any company on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
6 record, Nvidia has lost more than $2.5 trillion in market value, which The Kobeissi Letter calls the biggest 45-day loss for any stock in history.

The company said its 10-Q, the detailed quarterly filing, would come "in the coming weeks" instead of the same evening as usual, and the release mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.
Nvidia booked about $104 billion of revenue through its Singapore unit in 2025, roughly half its sales, the Financial Times reported.
Nvidia's customers are also taking longer to pay, with bills outstanding at 64 days of sales, the most since 2022.
"I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, after Jensen Huang's exit as CEO.

itens.titulo: Small caps: Safra coloca na carteira banco que pode disparar 80% e chegar a R$ 100; confira o portfólio
itens.descricao: Small caps: Safra coloca na carteira banco que pode disparar 80% e chegar a R$ 100; confira o portfólio Money Times
itens.texto:
Small caps: Safra coloca na carteira banco que pode disparar 80% e chegar a R$ 100; confira o portfólio
O Banco Safra promoveu uma série de alterações em sua carteira recomendada de small caps para novembro e dezembro. Saíram C&A (CEAB3), JSL (JSLG3), Cyrela (CYRE3) e Banco Inter (INBR34), enquanto passaram a integrar a seleção Banco Mercantil (BMEB4), IRB (IRBR3), Metalúrgica Gerdau (GOAU4) e Minerva (BEEF3).
O principal destaque é o Banco Mercantil. Com preço-alvo de R$ 100, a ação apresenta potencial de valorização de 81% em relação ao último fechamento.
Segundo os analistas, o banco deve se beneficiar do crescimento na originação de crédito consignado do INSS e da normalização gradual da portabilidade, fatores que tendem a melhorar a dinâmica dos negócios.
“Além disso, acreditamos que a revinculação pode reduzir estruturalmente a inadimplência no segmento, compensando a maior pressão sobre a qualidade dos ativos”, afirmam.
Outras inclusões
No caso do IRB, o Safra avalia que a companhia ainda apresenta crescimento modesto dos prêmios, mas negocia a múltiplos mais descontados do que outras seguradoras brasileiras.
Além disso, os elevados índices de solvência abrem espaço para um aumento do payout de dividendos nos próximos anos.
Já a inclusão da Metalúrgica Gerdau está ligada à exposição indireta à Gerdau (GGBR4). Segundo o banco, a siderúrgica vem entregando resultados consistentes e deve manter uma forte geração de caixa nos próximos anos.
Por fim, a entrada da Minerva é sustentada pelo valuation. Para o Safra, a companhia negocia com desconto em relação ao valor considerado justo para o atual ciclo de mercado.
“Temos boas perspectivas para os próximos resultados, apoiadas pelo crescimento da receita e por uma geração de caixa mais robusta”, destacam os analistas.
A empresa também é vista como uma forma de exposição à valorização do dólar, que encerrou a última quinta-feira próximo de R$ 5,90.
Desempenho
Entre outubro e novembro, a carteira de small caps do Safra recuou 33%, desempenho inferior ao do Índice Small Cap (SMLL), que caiu 29% no mesmo período.
No acumulado do ano, a carteira registra perda de 16%, ante recuo de 12,66% do índice de referência.

itens.titulo: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
itens.descricao: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis CNBC
trechos: Nvidia shares fell 12% on Friday, sliding for a seventh straight day as investors grew increasingly concerned about life after co-founder Jensen Huang.
The stock is poised to close lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest such stretch since 2008.
Shares of Nvidia are down 44% over the period, pushing the company's market cap down by $2.5 trillion.
The stock is now trading at around 9.3 times forward earnings, while Advanced Micro Devices is valued at 29 times profit for the next 12 months.
Once the most valuable company, now, at a market cap of $3.1 trillion, Nvidia is fourth behind Apple and Microsoft and Alphabet.
12, after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly a spy.
Even a better-than-expected earnings report, which included an increase to fiscal 2028 guidance, didn't stem the selling.
Interim CEO Colette Kress, the company's longtime CFO, projected revenue growth next fiscal year of 75%, and said that customers aren't going anywhere.

itens.titulo: Ripple’s CEO Says Investors Sold XRP and Bitcoin to Buy Anthropic Shares
itens.descricao: Ripple’s CEO Says Investors Sold XRP and Bitcoin to Buy Anthropic Shares Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse says investors dumped XRP and Bitcoin to buy into Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO, just as they did before SpaceX.
- XRP sank 28% and Bitcoin 25% in the month before Anthropic's listing, a steeper slide than the 21% each lost before SpaceX.
- After SpaceX's debut, crypto stalled for a month, then XRP gained 18% and Bitcoin 21% by day 90, so any rebound may come slowly.
- It sounds nuts, but SoFi is giving new Active Invest users up to $1,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started.
He points to a similar pattern that occurred before SpaceX went public in June 2026 and expresses optimism that the crypto market will recover.
Anthropic, an AI-focused company known for its Claude language model, priced its shares at $83, exceeding its initial range of $70 to $78, and successfully raised $81.3 billion.
This figure surpasses the $75 billion SpaceX raised at its listing, making it the largest IPO ever.
With Anthropic beginning its trading on November 19, does the data back up the Ripple CEO's view of the Anthropic IPO?
